title: The current Copernicus OSTIA SST reanalysis does not have the 1995 and 2002 CoralTemp steps, but it shifts at four of its own bias-reference changes (1988, 1992, 2012, 2017; 60S-60N, 1982-2026)
abstract: Question: NOAA CoralTemp v3.1, the SST behind Coral Reef Watch bleaching alerts, has mean steps on about 3 June 1995 and 17 July 2002 in its 1985-2002 part, which is the first Met Office OSTIA reanalysis (v1). Does the current Copernicus Marine OSTIA reanalysis (v2, SST_GLO_SST_L4_REP_OBSERVATIONS_010_011, 1981-2026) have these steps, and does it shift at its own documented bias-reference changes? Approach: we read all 16,344 daily OSTIA v2 fields (public 0.4-degree zarr view) at 43,200 points (60S-60N) and compared them with HadSST4.2, ERSSTv5, COBE-SST2, DOISST v2.1, CoralTemp and 210 moored buoys. We wrote the test plan first, fitted steps at the ten bias-reference dates of the product quality document with placebo dates, ran a blind break search and dated breaks with daily data. Results: OSTIA v2 does not have the 1995 and 2002 steps (-0.023 and -0.027 C at 30S-30N, placebo z -1.0 and -1.1; CoralTemp -0.084 and +0.063 on the same mask). But OSTIA v2 is 0.25-0.30 C too cold from 5 September to 13 October 1988, when it had no bias reference (z -11 to -17), 0.20-0.27 C too cold in July-December 1991 after Pinatubo, and it rises on 1 January 1992 when ATSR-1 becomes the reference. It falls by 0.055 C (60S-60N; 30S-30N 0.084) on 1 April 2012, when AATSR was lost, and rises by 0.061 C (30S-30N 0.120) on 1 January 2017 with SLSTR-A (z 3.6-5.1; same result against each in situ product, smaller at the assimilated buoys). The 1985-2024 trend excess over in situ data is small (+0.002 to +0.007 C per decade), but without the 2012 and 2017 steps 2016 becomes the third warmest year (not fifth), the 2016-2017 drop grows from -0.035 to -0.096 C and the 2005-2024 tropical trend falls by 12%. CoralTemp has no 1988 or 1991 artifact. Limitations: the in situ references share data; the daily dating of the 2012 and 2017 steps is clear only in the tropics; causes are inferred from documented dates; a 1983-1985 cold period is not explained; marine heatwave statistics were not recalculated.

Dotted lines: OSTIA v2 bias-reference changes (CMEMS QUID Table 4). CoralTemp steps in 1995 and 2002; OSTIA v2 does not, but it dips in 1988 and 1991 and is cold from April 2012 to December 2016.
